        If maps into N extend across short exact sequences whose quotient is cogenerated by N, the left perpendicular and the cogenerated modules form a torsion pair.

        An Euler dimension formula identifies both halves of the rigid kernel torsion pair. The division-ring actions are needed only on the two Hom spaces.

        theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.cogeneratedByModule_le_of_product_embedding {R : Type u} [Ring R] [IsArtinianRing R] {N M : ModuleCat R} {ι : Type u} (g : ↑N →ₗ[R] ι → ↑M) (hg : Function.Injective ⇑g) :
        cogeneratedByModule N ≤ cogeneratedByModule M

        An embedding of N in a product of copies of M transfers finite cogeneration tests, since finitely many coordinates separate an Artinian domain.

        theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.finite_perpendicular_or_generic_grain {R : Type u} [Ring R] (k : Type u) [Field k] [Algebra k R] (N : ModuleCat R) (he : IsEndofinite N) (hs : SplitsOnCogeneratedModules k N) {ι J : Type u} [Fintype J] (label : ι → J) (hl : Function.Surjective label) (D : J → ModuleCat R) (hd : ∀ (j : J), CategoryTheory.Indecomposable (D j)) (e : ↑N ≃ₗ[R] DirectSum ι fun (i : ι) => ↑(D (label i))) :

        The left perpendicular is represented by a finite module unless N has a generic grain summand.

        In the finite alternative, a single finite module realizes both halves of the pair.
